header:
Win a Car on TV?
Here's the Catch

lines.text: Win a $30,000 car, and you could owe $6,600.
lines.say: Win a thirty-thousand-dollar car, and you could owe sixty-six hundred.

lines.text: In 2004, Oprah's $28,500 free cars came with tax bills of up to $7,000.
lines.say: Sound dramatic? In 2004, Oprah's twenty-eight-thousand-five-hundred-dollar free cars came with tax bills of up to seven thousand dollars.

lines.text: The myth: a prize is free. The fact: the IRS counts it as income, at fair market value.
lines.say: Here's the myth: a prize is free. Here's the fact: the IRS counts it as income, at fair market value.

lines.text: And the show reports it to the IRS on a Form 1099-MISC.
lines.say: And the show reports it to the IRS on a ten ninety-nine form, so it doesn't slip by.

lines.text: Our math: a $30,000 car in a 22% bracket is $6,600 in federal tax.
lines.say: Our math: a thirty-thousand-dollar car in a twenty-two percent bracket means sixty-six hundred dollars in federal tax.

lines.text: Then add state income tax where it applies, plus possible sales tax, registration and insurance.
lines.say: Then add state income tax where it applies, plus possible sales tax, registration and insurance.

lines.text: The escape hatch: you can usually say no. Under IRS rules, a refused prize isn't income.
lines.say: The escape hatch? You can usually say no. Under IRS rules, a prize you refuse isn't income.

lines.text: So a free car still has a price tag. Rules vary, so check a tax pro.
lines.say: So remember, a free car still has a price tag. Rules vary, so check a tax pro.

post.title: You won a car on a game show. Here's the tax bill.
post.ig:
A free car from a game show can come with a tax bill in the thousands.
The IRS counts prizes as income at fair market value, and the show reports it on Form 1099-MISC.
Our math: a $30,000 car in a 22% bracket means $6,600 in federal tax, before state tax, sales tax, registration and insurance.
In 2004, Oprah's $28,500 free cars came with tax bills of up to $7,000 (CNN/Money).
You can usually refuse a prize, and a refused prize isn't income (IRS Pub 525).
Sources: IRS Publication 525, CNN/Money (2004), IRS 2026 tax brackets.
